item.title: 'A futuristic debate now very real': Why the world is struggling to regulate killer robots
item.description: Representatives from 128 nations are meeting in Geneva on Monday to decide whether to move ahead with negotiating legally binding rules around the use of AI-powered weapons that can kill without human involvement. FRANCE 24 spoke with artificial intelligence researcher Vincent Boulanin to find out just what is at stake.

item.title: Czech mass protests: Media is the first casualty 'when you want to attack democracy'
item.description: As hundreds of thousands of people gather in Prague to protest the Czech government's proposal to replace public broadcasting licence fees with direct state funding, Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Bára Stárek, Executive Director of Díky, že můžem. Stárek warns that the proposed changes offer "no real safeguards" against political influence, pointing to developments in Slovakia and Hungary. She also drew a parallel with the Velvet Revolution of 1989, recalling that "we didn't have a free media and we only had a state media" under communist rule. "Media is the first (line of) attack when you want to attack democracy," she said. With the legislation expected to reach Parliament in January, Stárek believes the demonstrations will continue if the government refuses to engage in any discussions.

item.title: U.N. talks seek to rein in 'killer robots' as fears over AI weapons grow
item.description: Countries are meeting in Geneva to negotiate rules on weapons that can select and kill targets without human intervention. But with the U.S., Russia and Israel resisting legally binding controls, campaigners fear the window to act is closing.

item.title: Russia's war on Ukraine: 'Americans want to have a deal whatever the cost for both Ukraine & Europe'
item.description: Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Grégoire Roos, Director of the Europe and Russia and Eurasia Programmes at Chatham House. As European countries prepare to take part in the next round of Ukraine peace talks, Roos questions whether having five European representatives could weaken their negotiating position. "The other option is to realize that it dilutes the negotiating power of Europe. And I would lean towards that," he says, proposing Finnish President Alexander Stubb as a possible representative. Roos also points to differences between Washington and European governments over negotiations with Russia. While "the Americans do absolutely want to have a deal whatever the cost for both Ukraine and Europe," he argues that European governments have little choice but to maintain pressure on Moscow, which has yet to abandon its "maximalist demands."

item.title: French film star Depardieu drops appeal against sexual conviction
item.description: French film star Gérard Depardieu on Monday dropped his appeal against a conviction for sexually assaulting two women during the filming of a movie in 2021 and issued "sincere apologies" for his past behaviour on set. "For a long time on film sets, I hid behind provocation and ribald humour," Depardieu, 77, said in the statement, withdrawing his appeal on the day it was set to go to trial. "I believed my remarks and some of my gestures would be without consequences" for those involved, he said. "They were not, particularly coming from a powerful figure such as I once was."

item.title: French troops in Ukraine 'wouldn't be a surprise'
item.description: French soldiers have been operating in Ukraine for several months, training Ukrainian troops and helping maintain military equipment, France 24's sister radio network Radio France Internationale (RFI) reported on Monday. While the deployment has not been confirmed, such a mission would not come as a surprise to many in Ukraine, reports France 24's correspondent in Kyiv Gulliver Cragg.

item.title: Prague: Thousands of Czechs rally against government media funding plan
item.description: Tens of thousands of Czechs rallied in Prague on Sunday, November 15, against a government plan to cut a public media fee and move funding to the state budget, a policy critics say would dent the broadcasters' independence and viability.

item.description: Authorities say a 500-foot Atlantic asphalt tanker collided into the American Heritage cruise ship on Friday, causing the ship to fall on its side and capsize in just 22 minutes.

item.title: Melissa Auf Der Maur: 90s rock memoirs and photographs
item.description: Melissa Auf Der Maur grew up in Montreal, the daughter of a feminist activist mother and a journalist-turned-politician father. At just 22, she joined Courtney Love’s band Hole as its bass player, going on to become a role model for young female fans – and not only female fans – of alternative rock. She later joined The Smashing Pumpkins before striking out on her own as a solo artist. She dropped by FRANCE 24 to talk to Marjorie Hache about the epic decade that brought the 20th century to a close.

item.title: Verdict due in French trial over triple murder linked to Marseille drug wars
item.description: In France, a highly anticipated verdict in a triple homicide is expected later today. Often called the Kessaci trial, the plight of the Kessaci family has drawn attention across France, the surviving brother Amine Kessaci has become an outspoken advocate against drug trafficking and in particular in Marseille.

item.title: Did France abandon its athletes after the Olympics?
item.description: Two years after hosting the Olympics, France seems to have lost interest in supporting its athletes. With budget cuts and lackluster interest from sponsors, some – despite their competitive successes – are turning to influencer work to finance their sport careers.

item.title: US to further curb China's access to Nvidia chips
item.description: The US government is set to further restrict China's access to the most powerful AI chips, such as the ones provided by tech giant Nvidia.

item.title: COP31 deal draft foreshadows difficult route to consensus
item.description: COP31 negotiators in Turkey released a draft agreement on Monday to advance talks on fossil fuels and climate finance before this week's deadline. The pressure to reach a deal is intense after a year of environmental challenges including catastrophic glacier flooding in Nepal and European wildfires, even as global conflict and cost-of-living protests distract leaders from climate action.

item.title: Saudi Arabia dismisses commander of anti-Houthi coalition as rebels advance
item.description: Saudi Arabia has removed the commander of the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen, state media said Monday, as the Iran-backed rebels advanced on the temporary capital of Aden. The shake up comes after Houthi forces took territory on Yemen's southern coast and Saudi-backed forces fell back to defend the capital.

item.title: 'Historical fiction is about filling in the gaps', author Ian McGuire says
item.description: A Man Booker Prize nominee has been speaking to FRANCE 24 about his latest novel and his passion for researching and writing historical fiction. Ian McGuire was shortlisted for the prize in 2016 for his novel “The North Water”. His latest book, “White River Crossing”, was published earlier this year and has now been translated into French, under the shortened title “White River”.

item.title: Musk among more than 150,000 calling for Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia
item.description: Could Jensen Huang make a stunning return to Nvidia just days after resigning as CEO of the AI chip giant over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy? The possibility is growing after Elon Musk and more than 158,000 others signed an open letter calling for Huang's reinstatement.

item.title: Russia says intercepted over 1,300 Ukrainian drones in a major attack
item.description: Russia intercepted 1,336 drones launched by Ukraine, Russia’s Defense Ministry said Monday, in what was the most claimed downings since Moscow’s all-out invasion of its neighbor nearly five years ago. Russia, meanwhile, has battered Ukrainian civilian areas with relentless strikes that seek to choke the economy and break public morale, in attacks President Volodymyr Zelensky said were made possible ⁠partly due to restrictions on Ukraine's use of SpaceX's Starshield service.

item.title: Israel's Netanyahu accused of electoral interference
item.description: Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot said on Sunday caretaker premier Benjamin Netanyahu must leave office immediately following reports of alleged electoral interference by a Netanyahu aide. France 24's Noga Tarnopolsky has the details.

item.title: Iran blocks UN nuclear site visits until war ends

The ministry's statement follows calls for the UN watchdog to resume inspections of nuclear sites, which have been suspended since last year's 12-day war with Israel.

item.title: Excitement builds ahead of GTA VI release

The game, founded nearly three decades ago and built around stealing cars and outrunning the police, boasts some 500 million sales, and this time is preparing for yet another big score, as millions of fans around the world get ready for its launch.
